input.title: Add toFahrenheit export
input.plan:
## Problem

`npm test` (`node --test`) fails at import time: `test/temperature.test.mjs:4` imports `{ toCelsius, toFahrenheit }` from `src/temperature.js`, but that module only exports `toCelsius`. The ESM linker throws before any test body runs, so all three tests error out.

## Change

Single file: `src/temperature.js`.

Add one exported function alongside the existing `toCelsius`, mirroring its style (JSDoc one-liner, rounding to one decimal):

```js
/** Celsius -> Fahrenheit, rounded to one decimal. */
export function toFahrenheit(c) {
  return Math.round((c * 9) / 5 * 10 + 320) / 10;
}
```

Formula: `c * 9/5 + 32`, equivalent to `(c * 9/5 + 32) * 10 / 10` after rounding. Written as `Math.round((c * 9) / 5 * 10 + 320) / 10` so the addition of 32 happens inside the rounded numerator — same structure as `toCelsius`'s `Math.round(... * 10) / 10`, and it avoids a separate intermediate rounding.

No other files change. No new test file — the existing test already covers the function.

## Why the round-trip test passes

The third test asserts `toFahrenheit(toCelsius(f)) === f` for `f` in `[-40, 68, 98.6]`. Checking by hand:

- `-40` → `toCelsius` = -40 → `toFahrenheit` = -40
- `68` → `toCelsius` = 20 → `toFahrenheit` = 68
- `98.6` → `toCelsius` = 37 → `toFahrenheit` = 98.6

All exact under the one-decimal rounding, so strict equality holds.

## Verification

1. `npm test` — expect 3 tests passing, 0 failing.
2. Spot-check the boundary values named in the failures (`toFahrenheit(0) === 32`, `toFahrenheit(100) === 212`) implicitly covered by step 1.
